samples.prompt: Some people support the proposal that universities should offer online classes alongside classroom lessons. Others believe practical difficulties should be addressed before it is introduced widely. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

samples.summaryVi: Học online giúp linh hoạt giờ học; cần thảo luận và hỗ trợ để tránh học một mình.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: There are different views about the proposal that universities should offer online classes alongside classroom lessons. Supporters emphasise its usefulness, while others believe that practical difficulties should be dealt with before it is introduced more widely. Both positions have reasonable concerns. In my opinion, the idea is worth supporting when those difficulties are addressed.
paragraphs.noteVi: Giới thiệu hai phía và ý kiến cá nhân.

parts.text: the idea is worth supporting when those difficulties are addressed.

paragraphs.label: Quan điểm thứ nhất
paragraphs.text: On the one hand, supporters focus on the benefits. One important point in favour of the proposal is that students can fit learning around work and family responsibilities. This is possible because recorded lessons can be watched again at a convenient time. For example, a student who works in a restaurant can review a morning lecture after the evening shift. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

paragraphs.text: On the other hand, a more cautious view deserves attention. A difficulty that should not be ignored is that some learners may feel isolated. This matters because a screen does not always make it easy to ask a quick question or form friendships. For instance, a first-year student may stop working on a difficult task instead of asking a classmate for help. The result may be frustration or a decision to stop taking part. This is not simply a question of people refusing to make an effort; practical conditions can prevent a reasonable idea from working as intended.

parts.text: a shop assistant can attend an evening computer class to learn how to manage simple spreadsheets. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

paragraphs.label: Quan điểm thứ hai
paragraphs.text: On the other hand, a more cautious view deserves attention. A difficulty that should not be ignored is that people with the greatest need may still be unable to attend. This matters because transport, childcare and changing work hours can create barriers. For instance, a parent may miss an evening class because there is no one available to look after a child. The result may be frustration or a decision to stop taking part. This is not simply a question of people refusing to make an effort; practical conditions can prevent a reasonable idea from working as intended.

paragraphs.label: Ý kiến của tôi
paragraphs.text: My own view is that the potential benefit is worth pursuing, but the conditions matter. In particular, it would be sensible to offer flexible schedules and simple support for attendance. People should be able to understand what is expected and raise difficulties before those difficulties become a reason to give up. A flexible plan is therefore more convincing than a promise that the same method will work equally well for everyone.

paragraphs.label: Kết bài
paragraphs.text: In conclusion, one side is right to recognise the potential value, while the other is right to ask how the idea will work in practice. I support a planned and flexible approach that pursues the benefit without overlooking the people who may face difficulties.
